newsitem.title: HONG KONG: INTERVIEW - Hongkong Bank keen and upbeat on China.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Hongkong Bank keen and upbeat on China.

text.p: Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp Ltd said on Monday it hoped to enjoy a privileged role in China in coming years while opportunities in its Hong Kong base should abound after the territory returns to Chinese rule.
"We see Hong Kong as a very good place to do business and a lot of opportunities are available and will be available after the handover," executive director Vincent Cheng said.
"Hong Kong will be the best place for us to launch our activities in China...We will be the largest foreign institution in China," he told Reuters in an interview.

Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp, also known as Hongkong Bank, is a unit of HSBC Holdings Plc. Established in Hong Kong in 1865, it is the largest bank incorporated in the territory and has repeatedly voiced an optimistic view on Hong Kong's change in sovereignty.
Britain will hand the affluent territory back to China on midnight June 30 after 156 years of colonial rule.
"I don't see any reason to suspect that China would want to change Hong Kong when Hong Kong is working so smoothly," said Cheng.
"We are also helping China to modernise in a tremendous way and I don't see any reason why the Chinese government would want to interfere with Hong Kong."
Cheng said Hong Kong should continue to be the main conduit for investment into China because it has the infrastructure already in place and people who understand the Chinese market.
"In Hong Kong, we have a large number of people full-time looking at China business and therefore they understand the opportunities and the risks."
"They can provide expertise to investors who are interested in the China market as well as the business connections so we will remain the major conduit of investment into China."
Mainland growth should continue at nine to 10 percent annually for at least the next several years while double-digit growth was expected in coastal regions, Cheng said.

Twenty percent of China's population was "highly bankable" and developments in the banking sector should provide a wealth of opportunities, particularly for Hongkong Bank whose long history there put it in an advantageous position, Cheng said.

"We have an excellent relationship with the Chinese government. They understand the bank, they respect the bank because we have demonstrated to everyone how successful we are and what sort of services we could provide to companies."
Hongkong Bank has seven branches and three representative offices in China. It plans to open another branch in the Pudong district of Shanghai this month which will do renminbi business.
"We have around 500 people in China itself which makes up by far the largest growing bank in China," Cheng said.
"The presence is still small because we are basically restricted by government regulations."
He said Hongkong Bank would continue to move into commercial and corporate banking on the mainland while expanding its debt and capital market activities.
Hongkong Bank's investment bank had been expanding rapidly in China and hoped to win approval soon for a representative office in Beijing, he added.

"In terms of branch network, I think we have to be realistic because at the moment branch licences are not easy to get. But in terms of treasury activities, in terms of corporate finance and other investment banking activities they are less restrictive and therefore I hope we will be able to see a lot more business in those two areas."
"I am truly confident that this group, if we are allowed to operate in China more freely than we are now, China will be a major growth area for us," he said.
"If they say we can have 200 branches, we will have 200 branches."
-- Hong Kong newsroom (852) 2843 6345
